name: Arabius Scholasticus
bio: Arabius Scholasticus is one of the epigrammatists whose short poems were gathered in the Greek Anthology. Paton's index of authors gives no firm date for the poet. Paton's index lists the poet among the writers of the Cycle of Agathias, the sixth-century anthology.
This archive carries the 1 epigram ascribed to the poet in the third volume of W. R. Paton's prose translation (Book IX: 667).

poems.title: Book IX, 667: On a Suburban Pleasaunce
poems.author: Arabius Scholasticus
poems.text: I am rich in waters, gardens, groves, vineyards, and the generous gifts of the neighbouring sea. Both the fisherman and the husbandman offer me pleasing presents from sea and land, and those who rest in me are soothed either by the song of birds or the sweet call of the ferryman.

poems.title: Book XVI, 39: On a Portrait of Longinus the Prefect in Byzantium
poems.author: Arabius Scholasticus
poems.text: The Nile, Persia, the Iberian, the Lycians, the West, Armenia, the Indians, the Colchians near the crags of Caucasus, and the burning plains of the widely-scattered Arabians, are witnesses to the rapidly executed labours of Longinus; and as he was on his journeys a swift minister of the Emperor, so likewise was he swift in giving us peace which had lain in hiding.

poems.title: Book XVI, 144: On Atalanta and Hippomenes
poems.author: Arabius Scholasticus
poems.text: Hast thou thrown this golden gift to the maiden, Hippomenes, as a wedding present, or to delay her fleet feet? The apple accomplished both, since it both delayed the girl in her course and was a token of Aphrodite, who links in wedlock.

poems.title: Book XVI, 148: On the Same
poems.author: Arabius Scholasticus
poems.text: Did Cepheus or the painter expose Andromeda on the rocks, for the judgment of the eye is indecisive And was the monster drawn as we see it on the curving crag, or did it rise out of the neighbouring sea? I see: a skilled man made these things; he was indeed clever thus to deceive our eyes and our wits.

poems.title: Book XVI, 149: On a Picture of Helen
poems.author: Arabius Scholasticus
poems.text: This is the lovely form of Argive Helen, whom of old the cowherd carried away, spurning Zeus who protects host and guest.

poems.title: Book XVI, 225: On a Statue of Pan
poems.author: Arabius Scholasticus
poems.text: We might, perhaps, have clearly heard Pan piping, for the sculptor infused breath into the statue, but left resourceless when he saw fickle Echo flying, the god renounced the unavailing voice of the pipe.

poems.title: Book XVI, 314
poems.author: Arabius Scholasticus
poems.text: The city could have afforded a golden statue for Longinus if august Justice did not loathe gold.

poems.title: On a Pan Piping (Mackail)
poems.author: Arabius Scholasticus
poems.collection: Select Epigrams from the Greek Anthology (1890)
poems.text: One might surely have clearly heard Pan piping, so did the sculptor mingle breath with the form; but in despair at the sight of flying, unstaying Echo, he renounced the pipe's unavailing sound.

poems.title: Palace Gardens (Mackail)
poems.author: Arabius Scholasticus
poems.collection: Select Epigrams from the Greek Anthology (1890)
poems.text: I am filled with waters and gardens and groves and vineyards, and the joyousness of the bordering sea; and fisherman and farmer from different sides stretch forth to me the pleasant gifts of sea and land: and them who abide in me either a bird singing or the sweet cry of the ferrymen lulls to rest.
